correctness.rationale: For n=2p^a q^b, p<q odd primes, sigma(n)/n=(3/2)(sum_{i=0}^a p^{-i})(sum_{j=0}^b q^{-j}). If p>=7 q>=11 then upper bound <=77/40<2; if p=5 q>=17 it is <=255/128<2; p=5,a=1,q=11 or13 gives upper bound <=99/50<2. Thus only p=3 or (5,7),(5,11),(5,13) remain. Every p=3 n is multiple of semiperfect 6. The lone squarefree odd-part case 70 has sigma=144 but is not semiperfect: an excluded set would total sigma−2n=4, whereas available proper divisors <=4 are only 1,2. Exact divisor-complement seed certificates: 350 exclusion 2+7+10+25=44; 490 exclusion 1+10+35=46; 550 exclusion 1+5+10=16; 650 exclusion 2=2. Complements of excluded proper divisors sum each seed. Semiperfectness passes to multiples, and all surviving families have one seed as divisor. Every proper divisor of the seeds is deficient or equals 70,110,130, all nonsemiperfect, so seeds are primitive. All other semiperfect members contain a proper semiperfect divisor. Independent subset-sum and classification checks for 495 parameter instances n<=15000 confirmed; proof applies to unbounded exponents.
